Let me analyze this OIML certificate markdown.

Document-level info:
- Certificate number: R49/2006-FR2-09.07 rev2
- Scheme: The cert doesn't explicitly state "Scheme A" or "Scheme B"... R49 certificates — this one doesn't mention scheme explicitly. I should omit or leave it out since not stated. Actually the schema says scheme (A|B). Since it's not mentioned, I'll omit it. Hmm, but rule 8 says don't fabricate. Omit.
- Member State: FRANCE
- Date issued: 2010-10-05 (05 October 2010)
- Issuing authority: Laboratoire National de Métrologie et d'Essais (LNE)
- Person responsible: Thomas LOMMATZSCH
- Title: Responsable du Pôle Certification / Measuring Instruments Division Manager
- Address: 1, rue Gaston Boissier - 75724 Paris Cedex 15
- Phone: 01 40 43 37 00
- Email: info@lne.fr
- Website: www.lne.fr

Applicant: ITRON ITALIA S.p.A, Strada Valcossera, 16, 14100 ASTI, ITALY
Manufacturer: ITRON ITALIA S.p.A, Strada Valcossera, 16, ITA, 14100 ASTI

Certified type: water meter ITRON type TMII, multi jet water meter
Category: "Water meter" — schema examples give "Gas meter" etc. Water meter fits.
Type designations: ["TMII"]
Description: "multi jet water meter ITRON type TMII intended for the measurement of cold water in the field of residential and commercial use."

Recommendation: R49 (OIML R49/2006). Canonical id "R49", edition 2006. Accuracy classes: the table says "Accuracy class 2" — that's for water meters (class 2 per R49). Include accuracy_classes: ["2"]? The recommendation accuracy_classes field — I think that's for the certificate's accuracy classes. R49 uses accuracy classes 1 and 2. The certified type has accuracy class 2. Include ["2"].

Test reports: 
- Report n°3283-3291 of 18 September 2009, 97 pages — role: evaluation_report (OIML R 49 EVALUATION REPORT)
- Report n°4279-4282 of 29 June 2010 ("20010" typo), 24 pages and 6 annexes

The test_reports schema: id, date, pages, role. 
- id: "3283-3291", date: "2009-09-18", pages: 97, role: "evaluation_report"
- id: "4279-4282", date: "2010-06-29", pages: 24, role: "evaluation_report"? Both are R49 evaluation reports. Maybe role "type_evaluation_report" for one... The schema lists roles: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. These are evaluation report(s). I'll use "evaluation_report" for both.

project_number: "Référence LNE-17628 rév. n° 1"? That's an internal reference. Hmm, project_number — could be "LNE-17628". I'll include project_number as "LNE-17628". Actually maybe safer to omit? The schema has project_number field. The reference "LNE-17628 rév. n° 1" is the certificate form reference. It could be a document reference rather than project number. I'll omit to avoid fabrication. Actually it says "Référence LNE-17628 rév. n° 1" — this is likely the internal form number. Omit.

page_total: appendix consists of 1 page. The schema's page_total is document-level page total. The certificate says appendix "comprend 1 page(s)". Include page_total: 1? Ambiguous. I'll include 1 since it states the appendix is 1 page. Hmm — actually page_total might mean total pages of the certificate. The certificate + appendix = presumably 2 pages, footer says "Page 1 / 1" for the annex. The annex is 1 page. I'll set page_total: 1 (the annex). Or omit. I'll include page_total: 1.

Now the metrological characteristics table. This is a matrix with two nominal diameters: 15 mm and 20 mm.

Table structure:
- Indicating device: Glass-metal or plastic (type level)
- Version: linear (type level)
- Nominal Diameter (mm): 15 | 20 → model-level attribute (two variants)
- Permanent flowrate Q3 (m³/h): 1.6 | 2.5
- Overload flowrate Q4 (m³/h): 2 | 3.125
- Orientation: Horizontal | All position | Horizontal | All position — interesting: 4 columns. For DN15: Horizontal (Q3/Q1=100), All position (Q3/Q1=31.5); for DN20: Horizontal (100), All position (31.5). So orientation is a config axis: orientation × model.
- Q3/Q1: 100 | 31.5 | 100 | 31.5
- Q2/Q1: 1.6 (type level)
- Accuracy class: 2 (type level)
- Temperature class: T30 (type level)
- Environmental class: C (type level)
- Flow disturbance sensitivity class: U0D0 (type level)
- Maximal admissible pressure (bar): 16 (type level)
- Pressure loss class: ΔP63 (type level)
- Connections: Threads (type level)
- Length (mm): 142…190 | 190 — ranges per model
- Cyclical volume (dm³): 29.543 | 41.156 (French decimals: 29,543 → 29.543)
- Indicating device range (m³): 99 999,99998 or 9 999,99998 — two alternatives: 99999.99998 or 9999.99998. This is a value list alternative. Could represent as value string or list. Rules say lists of values become model matrix... but here it's two options per unit, not per model. Hmm. I could represent as value: ["99999.99998", "9999.99998"]? Schema allows value: number | {min,max} | string. Maybe use string "99999.99998 or 9999.99998". That's simplest and honest.
- Verification scale (dm³): 0.02 (0,02 → 0.02)
- Reverse flow measurement: No (* footnote)

So model family: DN15 and DN20 variants. Also orientation config within each.

Model family models: 
- model_id "DN15" (attributes nominal_diameter 15)
- model_id "DN20"

Config axis: orientation (Horizontal vs All position) affecting Q3/Q1.

Q3/Q1 for Horizontal = 100, All position = 31.5. So config_level:
- attribute: q3_over_q1_ratio (or q3_q1_ratio), axis: orientation, values: [{condition: "Horizontal", value: 100}, {condition: "All position", value: 31.5}]

Actually per R49, ratios below listed values permitted but not below 10 (footnote). The footnote marker: the text says "* For a given nominal flowrate (Q3) values of Q3/Q1 lower than those listed in the table above are permitted. However the values of this ratio cannot be below 10."

Footnotes:
- marker "*" (or "1") — the table uses "*" for Reverse flow measurement, but there are two footnote texts: one single-asterisk and one double-asterisk. The markdown shows "\* *For a given nominal flowrate (Q3) values of Q3/Q1...below 10.*" and "\*\* *This meter is not designed to measure reverse flow...*". But in the table only "Reverse flow measurement *" has a marker. Hmm — the first footnote seems misattached; it belongs to Q3/Q1. The second (** obviously attaches to Reverse flow measurement.

I'll extract footnotes:
- {"marker": "*", "text": "For a given nominal flowrate (Q3) values of Q3/Q1 lower than those listed in the table above are permitted. However the values of this ratio cannot be below 10."}
- {"marker": "**", "text": "This meter is not designed to measure reverse flow but can withstand accidental reverse flow without deterioration or change in its metrological properties for forward flow."}

And attach "**" footnote marker to reverse_flow_measurement value "No". Also attach "*" to q3_q1_ratio values? The table doesn't show the marker on Q3/Q1 row, but the footnote text clearly references it. To be safe, attach footnote_markers ["*"] to the q3_q1_ratio config values and ["**"] to reverse flow measurement value.

Now matrix_tables: should I emit the full table as a matrix_table? The R137 example says emit matrix_tables AND model_level. Here the table is a 2-D (model × attribute) layout. I'll emit a matrix_table "Metrological characteristics" with columns and rows... The table rows here are attributes and columns are models (15, 20), plus orientation sub-columns. It's transposed relative to R137 example. I could structure rows as models:

columns: ["nominal_diameter_mm", "permanent_flowrate_q3_m3/h", ...]. Let me create:

matrix_tables:
- name: "Metrological characteristics"
- columns: ["nominal_diameter", "q3", "q4", "orientation", "q3_q1_ratio", "q2_q1_ratio", "accuracy_class", "temperature_class", "environmental_class", "flow_disturbance_sensitivity_class", "map", "pressure_loss_class", "connections", "length", "cyclical_volume", "indicating_device_range", "verification_scale_interval", "reverse_flow_measurement"]

Hmm, that's awkward. Alternatively keep the table as rows per attribute. The schema says rows[] object per row. I could do rows keyed by model with orientation variants:

rows:
- {nominal_diameter_mm: 15, orientation: "Horizontal", q3: 1.6, q4: 2, q3_q1: 100, length_mm: {min:142,max:190}, cyclical_volume_dm3: 29.543}
- {nominal_diameter_mm: 15, orientation: "All position", q3: 1.6, q4: 2, q3_q1: 31.5, length_mm: {min:142,max:190}, cyclical_volume_dm3: 29.543}
- {nominal_diameter_mm: 20, orientation: "Horizontal", q3: 2.5, q4: 3.125, q3_q1: 100, length_mm: 190, cyclical_volume_dm3: 41.156}
- {nominal_diameter_mm: 20, orientation: "All position", q3: 2.5, q4: 3.125, q3_q1: 31.5, length_mm: 190, cyclical_volume_dm3: 41.156}

With column_units. That's reasonable. And type-level attributes as description: indicating device glass-metal or plastic, version linear, etc.

characteristics.type_level:
- indicating_device: {value: "Glass-metal or plastic"}
- device_version / version: {value: "linear"}
- q2_over_q1_ratio (Q2/Q1 = 1.6): value 1.6
- accuracy_class: {value: "2"} or 2? Class is nominal — I'd use value 2 numeric? Accuracy class "2" — treat as number 2. Fine.
- temperature_class: {value: "T30"}
- environmental_class: {value: "C"}
- flow_disturbance_sensitivity_class: {value: "U0D0"}
- maximum_admissible_pressure (MAP): value 16, unit bar
- pressure_loss_class: {value: "ΔP63"} — hmm, no LaTeX. ΔP63 is fine, it's an actual class label. Canonical label pressure_loss_class, value "DP63"? Keep "ΔP63" — it's not LaTeX, it's Unicode Δ. Fine.
- connections: {value: "Threads"}
- verification_scale_interval? "Verification scale (dm³)": 0,02 → value 0.02, unit "dm³". Actually for water meters R49, this is the verification scale interval. Label: verification_scale — keep as "verification_scale" per table text. I'll use verification_scale (canonical from the label "Verification scale"). Or "verification_scale_interval". The label is "Verification scale (dm³)". I'll use "verification_scale".
- reverse_flow_measurement: value "No", footnote_markers ["**"]
- indicating_device_range (m³): "99 999,99998 or 9 999,99998" → two values: 99999.99998 and 9999.99998. Since it's alternatives, I'll use value as string "99999.99998 or 9999.99998"? Or maybe a value list is not allowed per schema (value is number|{min,max}|string). Hmm. I could record value: "99999.99998", and note alternative? Better: value: "99999.99998 or 9999.99998" with unit "m³". That preserves it. I'll do that.

characteristics.model_level:
- nominal_diameter: unit mm, values: {model: "DN15", value: 15}, {model: "DN20", value: 20}
- permanent_flowrate_q3: unit m³/h, values 1.6 / 2.5
- overload_flowrate_q4: unit m³/h, values 2 / 3.125
- length: unit mm, values {min:142, max:190} / 190
- cyclical_volume: unit dm³, values 29.543 / 41.156

characteristics.config_level:
- attribute q3_over_q1 (Q3/Q1), axis: orientation, values: [{condition:"Horizontal", value:100}, {condition:"All position", value:31.5}] with footnote_markers ["*"] maybe.

Model family:
- family_name: "TMII"? The type is TMII. Models: DN15, DN20. Family name could be "TMII". The schema: family_name explicit family name if any, else null. "ITRON type TMII" — the family is TMII with DN15/DN20 variants. I'll set family_name "TMII".

Model entries with attributes:
- {"model_id": "DN15", "label": "ITRON TMII DN15", "attributes": {"nominal_diameter_mm": 15, "q3_m3h": 1.6}} — keep attributes simple.

Recommendation: {id: "R49", edition: 2006, scheme: ...}. Edition: R49/2006 → 2006. Accuracy classes: ["2"]. Scheme — OIML R49 certificates can be under scheme A or B per the certificate scheme definition; not mentioned here. Omit scheme in recommendation? The recommendation schema has scheme field — but not given; omit. Also certificate.scheme — omit.

Certificate number: "R49/2006-FR2-09.07 rev2". Include revision in number or separate? Keep full "R49/2006-FR2-09.07 rev2". Actually "rev2" — revision history? There's no explicit revision history section (changes). The "rev2" is part of cert numbering. revision_history: omit (no changes described).

oiml_issuer_id: not given. Omit.

page_total: 1? The certificate body plus 1-page annex. The footer says Page 1/1 for the annex. I'll set page_total: 1. Hmm, document-level page_total — certificate consists of main page + annex 1 page. The statement: "appendix ... consists of 1 page(s)". I'll include 1.

Issuing authority address: "1, rue Gaston Boissier, 75724 Paris Cedex 15". address_lines: ["1, rue Gaston Boissier", "75724 Paris Cedex 15"]. Phone "01 40 43 37 00", email "info@lne.fr", website "www.lne.fr". Person responsible: Thomas LOMMATZSCH, title: "Responsable du Pôle Certification" (Measuring Instruments Division Manager). Use English: "Measuring Instruments Division Manager" or keep French? Multilingual rule: extract English. The title given in English: "Measuring Instruments Division Manager". I'll use that, or include French. I'll use "Measuring Instruments Division Manager".

Member state: FRANCE.

Category: "Water meter".

Module designation: not applicable — omit or null. Schema: module_designation "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. For water meters, modules concept applies (R49 has modules too) but not mentioned → omit.

Component: indicating device is named: "Glass-metal or plastic". That's a sub-assembly alternative! components[] entry: role "indicating device", type_designations ["Glass-metal", "Plastic"], alternatives "OR". Good.

Indicating device range: two options 99 999,99998 m³ or 9 999 999,998? Wait "99 999,99998" = 99,999.99998 m³ and "9 999,99998" = 9,999.99998 m³. These correspond to the two indicating device types possibly. Record as string alternatives.

Date issued: 2010-10-05.

Now let me also consider "Temperature class T30" — cold water up to 30°C.

Accuracy classes: ["2"] — as numbers or strings? I'll use [2] numeric or ["2"]. Classes are labels; use [2]? I'll use ["2"]? Hmm. R49 accuracy classes are 1 and 2. I'll use [2].
